cohort: The cohort consisted of 226 mothers with rheumatic diseases (Systemic Lupus Erythematosus or other rheumatic diseases) who had 263 singleton deliveries.
finding: Preeclampsia was associated with longer maternal hospital stays and adverse infant outcomes including earlier delivery (average 3.3 weeks earlier), a 4-fold increased likelihood of preterm birth, and twice the likelihood of NICU admission.
